$comment: Shared VfProgressBar cases. Plain data only. The vocabulary is the historical Vue contract at fd793696f50d3be0fcd3788f0f8f751c63869963. This catalog is the bar's, not VfProgressSpinner's: the two share the role name and the tone union and nothing else, and contracts/progress-spinner/cases.json must never stand in for it - a spinner case has no value, no maximum, no fill and no label, so a catalog derived from it would measure a tone and a name and call it progress. Six dimensions are real: the value (zero, mid, full, overflow, negative, fractional, tiny), the maximum (default, custom, zero, negative, fractional, below one), the determinate/indeterminate branch (explicit, with an ignored value, composed), the visible label (shown, rounded, zero, beside a custom name), the consumer contract (class order, style merge, the custom property overridden, a role, a name, a labelledby, each aria-value attribute and aria-valuetext replacing or joining the component's own, aria-hidden, product data), and the paint (eight tones, stripes, height forms). Every case declares zero component-owned controls and no consumer control, because the bar has no slot.

propVocabulary.value: number, default 0. Non-finite is 0; otherwise clamped into [0, max]. Written as aria-valuenow and, as a ratio of max, as the fill's inline-size - both serialised as JavaScript serialises a number.
propVocabulary.max: number, default 100. Kept when finite and greater than zero; zero, a negative, NaN, Infinity and a numeric string fall back to 100. Written as aria-valuemax.
propVocabulary.indeterminate: boolean, default false. Adds vf-progress-bar--indeterminate, drops aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow, drops the fill's inline-size and hides the visible label. The stylesheet animates the fill.
propVocabulary.label: string, default "Progress". Written verbatim as aria-label on the root; an empty string is written empty, not dropped. Not the visible percentage.
propVocabulary.height: string | number, default undefined. Written as the --vf-progress-bar-height custom property: a number becomes pixels, a string passes through, absent writes nothing so the theme token applies, and an empty string writes no declaration either.
propVocabulary.showValue: boolean, default false. Renders span.vf-progress-bar__label inside the fill with the ratio rounded half-up to a whole percent, while determinate only.
propVocabulary.tone: One of neutral | primary | success | info | warn | help | danger | contrast, default primary. Selects the root modifier (none at primary, one for every other value including neutral). Never changes the role.
propVocabulary.animated: boolean, default false. Adds vf-progress-bar--animated only beside striped; alone it emits nothing.

cases.title: A bare bar: value 0 of 100, an empty fill, named Progress, sized by the theme token
An explicit zero, which is written as aria-valuenow=0 and inline-size 0% rather than dropped
A mid-range value: half the track and aria-valuenow=50
One of three: an unrounded 33.33333333333333% width beside aria-valuemax=3 and aria-valuenow=1
The maximum: a full track and aria-valuenow=100
A value above the maximum, clamped to it on both the attribute and the width
A negative value, clamped to zero on both the attribute and the width
Seven of twelve: aria-valuemax=12, aria-valuenow=7 and a 58.333333333333336% fill
Fifteen of twelve, clamped to twelve
A zero maximum, which falls back to 100 rather than dividing by zero: 5 of 100
A negative maximum, which falls back to 100: 5 of 100
A fractional value kept unrounded on the attribute and the width
A fractional maximum and value, whose ratio carries the floating-point residue into the width
A value clamped to a maximum below one: aria-valuemax=0.5, aria-valuenow=0.5, a full track
A value below 1e-6, which reaches aria-valuenow and the width in exponent form
An indeterminate bar: the modifier, no aria-value* attribute, no inline size, the stylesheet sweep
A value, a maximum and showValue passed beside indeterminate, all of which are ignored
An indeterminate info bar with stripes, so the modifiers are measured together
The visible percentage inside the fill
A 12.5% fill whose visible label reads 13% while aria-valuenow stays 1
A visible 0% label on an empty fill
A visible percentage beside a custom accessible name: the label is not the name
A custom accessible name
An empty accessible name: the attribute is present and empty, not absent
A numeric height, written as pixels into the custom property
A zero height, which is a length rather than an absence: the track collapses
A string height, passed through verbatim
An empty-string height, which writes no declaration and sizes exactly like the default
The neutral tone: the modifier a badge-derived rule would suppress
The primary tone: named explicitly, which emits no modifier and renders exactly like the default
The success tone
The info tone
The warn tone
The help tone
The danger tone
The contrast tone
A striped fill
animated without striped, which emits no modifier: there are no stripes to move
Animated stripes, which the stylesheet moves and reduced motion stops
A consumer class, appended after the block class
A consumer class after a tone and a stripe modifier, so the order of all four is measured
A consumer style beside no height declaration of the component's own
A consumer style merged after the component's height declaration
A consumer declaration of the height property, which wins over the prop
A consumer role, which replaces progressbar while the value attributes stay
A consumer aria-label, which replaces the label prop's name
A consumer aria-labelledby pointing at a heading, which names the bar over its own aria-label
A consumer aria-valuenow of 40 on a bar painted at 50%: the attribute is replaced, the fill is not
A consumer aria-valuemax, which replaces the resolved maximum on the attribute only
A consumer aria-valuemin, which replaces the fixed zero floor
A consumer aria-valuetext, forwarded beside the numeric value
A consumer aria-valuenow on an indeterminate bar, forwarded rather than stripped, with no range beside it
A consumer aria-hidden on the root: the bar leaves the tree while keeping its role attribute
A product data attribute and an id, forwarded onto the root and never onto the fill
Everything at once: 64 of 80, danger, animated stripes, a visible label, a 16px track, a custom name, a consumer class, style and data attribute
